question: What substance is released after a hemorrhage and causes an increase in the renal reabsorption of Na + ?:
reasoning_chain: CHAIN: "Hemorrhage" -> "Decreased blood volume" -> "Activation of the renin-angiotensin-aldosterone system" -> "Release of aldosterone" -> "Increased renal reabsorption of Na+" -> Aldosterone -> 95%

CHAIN: "Hemorrhage" -> "Decreased blood pressure" -> "Activation of the renin-angiotensin system" -> "Conversion of angiotensinogen to angiotensin I" -> "Conversion of angiotensin I to angiotensin II" -> "Increased renal reabsorption of Na+" -> Angiotensin II -> 90%
analysis: After a hemorrhage, the substance released that causes an increase in the renal reabsorption of Na+ is Aldosterone.
